newsitem.title: FRANCE: Suez, Lyonnaise merger said in final phase.
newsitem.headline: Suez, Lyonnaise merger said in final phase.

text.p: French newspaper La Tribune said on Friday sources within Lyonnaise des Eaux and Suez had confirmed plans to merge the two French groups were in the final stages and should be announced on Wednesday.

"Yesterday, there was confirmation from within both groups that the plan was in the final stages, the main obstacles now having been lifted," it said. The merger was likely to take the form of an absorption by Lyonnaise of the larger Suez, it said.
While not citing sources on this, the paper said the deal could be an exchange of two Suez shares for one Lyonnaise share, with a big exceptional dividend payout to lure Suez holders.

"One of the possible solutions would be to carry out an exceptional dividend payout ahead of the merger to Suez shareholders from the Astorg Street group's (Suez) treasury, which currently stands at five billion francs," the paper said.
"The size of the payout would depend on the share swap terms finally decided," it said.

It said it had got confirmation from some of Suez holders that they would react positively, saying Credit Agricole -- holder in both groups -- was in favour, and also Axa-UAP and Saint-Gobain. BNP had yet to take a stance, it added.

The newspaper also said Belgian businessmann Albert Frere, who owns a stake in Suez through holding company Electrafina, could take advantage of merger operation to boost his hold on Societe Generale de Belgique (SGB) by transfering his 12.4 percent stake in rival Banque Bruxelles Lambert to SGB.
The French stock market has, for well over a week, been betting on the deal going ahead.

Suez, a conglomerate which has lacked a clear identity since sale of Banque Indosuez to Credit Agricole, has a board meeting next week and will publish annual results next Wednesday, while Lyonnaise too meets to approve results for publication on Thursday.
